name: Dry Savanna Grass Tuft
creation_method: procedural Blender Python; painted blade atlas generated in code

source.license: Original procedural model and texture; no external assets used

variants.how: multiply the base colour (material colour factor or shader uniform) by these RGB values; height scaling is done in the game
variants.regrowing_note: also scale the instance height to about 0.4

wind.attribute: TEXCOORD_1 (uv1 in three.js): x = sway weight (0 at base, 1 at tip), y = per-blade phase 0..1
wind.node_animation: none; instance thousands of tufts with InstancedMesh and move vertices in the shader

shared.origin: tuft base centre at the world origin, Z up in Blender, Y up in glTF
shared.size_m: about 1.0 m wide and 0.7 m tall (blades lean outward); stalks on the high tier reach about 1.2 m
shared.material: one matte painted material, double sided, no alpha (shape comes from the geometry)
shared.instancing: one draw call per tier; use InstancedMesh with random yaw and scale 0.8-1.45

review_notes: Judge the painted look in the field preview, not only the single tuft.
Check blade shapes and tint variants against the game ground colours and moods.
Test shader wind and InstancedMesh in the game once 10 assets exist.

verification.method: GLB files re-read from disk after export
checks_passed: triangle count in each GLB equals the count built (110 / 252 / 455)
embedded atlas is a valid 256x512 JPEG, 29,311 bytes, not blank (read-back spread 0.247)
wind mask TEXCOORD_1 spans 0..1 in x; COLOR_0 and custom normals present
tint variants rendered and checked visually (dry, green, burned, regrowing)
260 instanced medium tufts rendered as a field to judge the painted look at distance

known_limits: Not tested in the game; shader wind and InstancedMesh are untested until 10 assets exist.
Tints are multipliers applied in the game; the game must implement them.
Blades are single-sided cards rendered double sided; check overdraw with very dense fields on weak phones.
